description:
How people get around and get online: households with no vehicle available, as a count and a share ([B25044](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25044)); commute mode shares for driving alone, public transportation, walking or cycling, and working from home ([B08301](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B08301)); the share of commutes of 45 minutes or more ([B08303](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B08303)); and the shares of households with no internet access and no computing device ([B28002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B28002), [B28001](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B28001)).

Curated indicators for all **32,612** incorporated places and census designated places in the United States, Puerto Rico and the island areas, from the U.S. Census Bureau's [American Community Survey](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs.html) **2020–2024 5-year estimates** (`acsdt5y2024`, the table-based [Summary File](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/summary_file/2024/table-based-SF/data/5YRData/)). The Census Bureau calls the ACS "the premier source of detailed information about the nation's people and housing". The Bureau publishes 1-year estimates only for places of 65,000 people or more, so the 5-year release is the only one that covers all 32,612 of them ([areas published](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/geography-acs/areas-published.html)).

Every estimate ships with its margin of error — `<column>_moe`, at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes — and the headline statistics also carry a coefficient of variation (`<column>_cv` = `moe / 1.645 / estimate`) so small-area noise can be flagged rather than mapped as if certain. Derived percentages propagate error with the Census Bureau's own formulas from [ACS Accuracy of the Data](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/tech_docs/accuracy/MultiyearACSAccuracyofData2024.pdf): sums add in quadrature, proportions use the subset formula with the ratio formula as fallback. ACS jam values for suppressed or unestimable cells are NULL here, never numbers, and medians are published as the Bureau publishes them — a median cannot be aggregated to a larger area. Each column's description names its ACS table, its exact universe, and the lines summed to make it.

Most of the 32,612 rows are small: the file holds every incorporated place and every [census designated place](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/bas/information/cdp.html) the Census Bureau delineates, from New York city to villages of 40 people, so filter on `population` before reading a place-level distribution as if every row were a city. A place is also not a partition of the country: the land between places is not in this file at all, so place rows do not sum to a county or a state. These are the noisiest estimates in this group: `pct_hh_no_vehicle` has a median coefficient of variation of **0.526**, and `pct_commute_transit` **0.691** over the 8,538 places that publish one at all (measured).

Geometries are the Census Bureau's [2024 cartographic boundary files](https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/cartographic-boundary.html) for incorporated places and census designated places (GENZ2024, 1:500,000), reprojected to EPSG:4326 and joined on `GEOID`. Cartographic rather than TIGER/Line because TIGER extends census geographies into open water while the cartographic files clip to the shoreline, which is what a choropleth wants. The boundary vintage matches the estimate vintage.

The join is driven by geometry, so a geography with 2024 boundaries but no ACS tabulation keeps its row with NULL values instead of disappearing: 279 places (MP 135, AS 77, GU 57, VI 10) in the island areas, which have cartographic boundaries but no ACS 5-year estimates because the Island Areas run a separate decennial-only program. Two more, Brentwood CDP and Wyandanch CDP, have boundaries and no matching ACS row, both in Suffolk County, New York — the county whose 2024 re-delineation also leaves 14 tracts and 39 block groups without ACS rows elsewhere in this catalog. One more: `2148000` Louisville city, Kentucky, which the boundary file still carries and the ACS tabulates as the consolidated `2148006` Louisville/Jefferson County metro government (balance) instead — so the Louisville you want is `2148006`. Keeping these rows means a national map has no holes and a consumer can see the absence; dropping them would make "every US geography" quietly mean something narrower.

This is one themed chunk of six at this geography. The other themes are [Income & Poverty](../place-income/collection.json), [People & Education](../place-people/collection.json), [Housing & Rent](../place-housing/collection.json) and [Health, Disability & Income by Race](../place-wellbeing/collection.json), split that way so a consumer who wants one theme reads one file. Chunks at the same geography hold the same rows and the same geometry, so they join 1:1 on `geoid`. A sixth collection, [All Indicators](../places/collection.json), carries all 112 columns on the same rows in one wide table — at this many features width costs little, so take that one if a question crosses themes. A place nests in a state but not in a county — a place can straddle a county line — so `substr(geoid, 1, 2)` reaches the state row and nothing else joins by prefix. Every other geography in this catalog is organized the same way — [block groups](../../block-groups/catalog.json), [census tracts](../../tracts/catalog.json), [counties](../../counties/catalog.json), [states](../../states/catalog.json), [ZCTAs](../../zctas/catalog.json) and [congressional districts](../../congressional-districts/catalog.json) — and the [blocks](../../blocks/collection.json) collection carries 2020 Decennial counts, a different survey and vintage rather than a finer version of these numbers.

The PMTiles archive is a census-geography pyramid built with [tylertoo](https://github.com/geoparquet-io/tylertoo): z0–z5 are county polygons carrying the Census Bureau's own published county estimates, and z6–z12 are the places themselves. Places do not nest inside counties — a place can cross a county line — so the county band is orientation at national zooms, not a roll-up of these features. Thinning this many polygons down to a national zoom would show a biased subset (small urban geographies drop first) rather than less data, so the coarse zooms step up to a coarser census geography instead of a thinned sample of this one. Every band carries the same column names, so one style expression classifies every zoom — but below z6 you are looking at counties, not places, and the values there are the Bureau's official estimates for those geographies, with their own meaning, rather than a visualization-only average: clicking a coarse feature identifies a real county by `geoid` and `name`. The `*_moe` columns are excluded from the tiles at every zoom — a margin of error is computed for one specific geography and cannot be carried across bands — while the `*_cv` columns are kept. Statistics come from the GeoParquet, never from the tiles.

This is a mirror — [data.census.gov](https://data.census.gov/) is authoritative, and nothing here is an official Census Bureau product. The exact upstream files this collection was built from are published as `source` assets, linked at their original census.gov URLs, so the original is always one click away; the Bureau's own documentation is linked alongside them. Read the collection's [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) before querying: it carries the schema, the join keys, the NULL-rate story and tested queries against the published URLs.

styles/default.title: No home internet
styles/default.description: Share of households with no internet subscription of any kind, pale to deep blue. Measured over all 31,711 places with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at 2%/5.5%/9.5%/15%/24%, which fall at the 19th/39th/60th/79th/91st percentile of the national distribution. 66.72% of places have a coefficient of variation above 0.3 at this geography, too many to fade without washing the map out, so read pct_no_internet_moe in the GeoParquet before drawing a conclusion from any single place.

styles/no-vehicle.title: Households without a vehicle
styles/no-vehicle.description: Share of households with no vehicle available, pale yellow through teal to navy. Measured over all 31,711 places with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at 0.5%/2.5%/5%/8.5%/14%, which fall at the 25th/40th/59th/77th/90th percentile of the national distribution. 60.43% of places have a coefficient of variation above 0.3 at this geography, too many to fade without washing the map out, so read pct_hh_no_vehicle_moe in the GeoParquet before drawing a conclusion from any single place.

styles/transit-commute.title: Commute by public transit
styles/transit-commute.description: Share of workers commuting by public transportation, pale yellow to dark green; the first class is deliberately narrow because most of the country has effectively none. Measured over all 31,433 places with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at 0.5%/2%/5%/10%/25%, which fall at the 80th/90th/95th/98th/100th percentile of the national distribution. 22.51% have a coefficient of variation above 0.3 and render faded — the estimate is real but its margin of error swamps it.

styles/work-from-home.title: Work from home
styles/work-from-home.description: Share of workers whose usual commute is none — they worked from home — pale lilac to deep purple. Measured over all 31,433 places with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at 1.5%/5.5%/10%/16%/25%, which fall at the 20th/39th/60th/78th/91st percentile of the national distribution.

doc-geo-tallies.title: 2020 Census national geographic entity tallies
doc-geo-tallies.description: The published count of every geographic entity type, which this collection's row count is checked against: 33,791 ZCTAs (33,642 US + 132 Puerto Rico + 17 island areas), 19,734 incorporated places and 12,454 census designated places, 441 congressional districts (436 US including the DC delegate + 1 Puerto Rico + 4 island areas). Index page: https://www.census.gov/geographies/reference-files/time-series/geo/tallies.html.

doc-cdp-about.title: Census Designated Places (CDPs) — Census Bureau
doc-cdp-about.description: How the Bureau delineates the unincorporated communities that make up roughly two fifths of the rows here, and how a CDP differs from an incorporated place.

doc-acs-handbook.title: Understanding and Using American Community Survey Data — Census Bureau handbooks
doc-acs-handbook.description: The Bureau's own guidance on what ACS estimates can and cannot support: 1-year versus 5-year releases, margins of error, comparing across vintages, and small-area reliability. Read it before drawing a conclusion from a single block group.

doc-acs-accuracy.title: ACS Accuracy of the Data (2024, multiyear estimates)
doc-acs-accuracy.description: The source of every margin-of-error formula this build applies: quadrature for sums, the proportion formula and its ratio fallback for percentages, and the definition of the published 90% confidence level.

doc-acs-subject-definitions.title: ACS 2024 Subject Definitions
doc-acs-subject-definitions.description: The Census Bureau's definitions of the concepts behind these columns — household, householder, gross rent, poverty status determined, group quarters, means of transportation to work, disability. Where a column description here says what a universe is, this is the document it is saying it from.

doc-geo-glossary.title: Census Bureau geography program glossary
doc-geo-glossary.description: Definitions of the geographies and the identifiers used here — block, block group, tract, county equivalent, GEOID, and what nests inside what.

table:columns.name: geoid
table:columns.description: 7-character place GEOID — state FIPS (2) + place FIPS (5), e.g. `0644000` for Los Angeles city. `substr(geoid, 1, 2)` is the state FIPS code, which is the only prefix join a place supports: places nest in states but not in counties (a place can straddle a county line) and a place is not a census-tract aggregate. Matches `GEOID` in the 2024 cartographic boundary place file; the ACS `1600000US` prefix is stripped.

table:columns.name: name
table:columns.description: Human-readable name from the cartographic boundary place file: `NAMELSAD`, `STATE_NAME` — "Los Angeles city, California", "Brentwood CDP, New York". `NAMELSAD` carries the legal/statistical descriptor, so the name itself says whether a place is a city, town, village, borough or CDP.

table:columns.name: state
table:columns.description: Two-letter USPS state or territory code (`MO`, `PR`, `GU`). Carried on every collection from the `STATEFP → USPS` lookup embedded in `tools/specs.py` rather than read off the boundary files, because the 2024 cartographic boundary block-group file has no `STUSPS` column while the tract, county and state files do.

table:columns.name: population
table:columns.description: Total population. Universe: total population. The single line of [B01003](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B01003) (Total Population), published as an integer. Carried on every ACS collection so a rate can be weighted or sanity-checked without a second download. NULL on 0.86% of places — the 282 places with 2024 boundaries but no ACS row: 279 in the island areas (MP 135, AS 77, GU 57, VI 10), Brentwood CDP and Wyandanch CDP in Suffolk County, New York, and Louisville city, Kentucky, whose ACS tabulation is the consolidated `2148006` Louisville/Jefferson County metro government (balance).

table:columns.name: population_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `population` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Component margins add in quadrature — `sqrt(Σ moe²)` — which is the Census Bureau's formula for the margin of a sum. NULL when every component is a jam value.

table:columns.name: aland_sqkm
table:columns.description: Land area in square kilometres, rounded to 3 decimals. `ALAND / 1e6` from the cartographic boundary file. Land only: water area is excluded, which is what makes it the right denominator for population density.

table:columns.name: pop_density
table:columns.description: People per square kilometre of land area, rounded to 1 decimal: `population / aland_sqkm`. NULL where `ALAND` is 0 or `population` is NULL.

table:columns.name: hh_no_vehicle
table:columns.description: Occupied housing units with no vehicle available, owner- and renter-occupied combined. Universe: occupied housing units. Lines 3 + 10 of [B25044](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25044) (Tenure by Vehicles Available) — the "No vehicle available" line under each tenure — which is what makes this a tenure-blind count. Published as an integer; the two margins of error add in quadrature.

table:columns.name: hh_no_vehicle_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `hh_no_vehicle` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Component margins add in quadrature — `sqrt(Σ moe²)` — which is the Census Bureau's formula for the margin of a sum. NULL when every component is a jam value.

table:columns.name: pct_hh_no_vehicle
table:columns.description: Percent of occupied housing units with no vehicle available. Universe: occupied housing units. Lines 3 + 10 over line 1 of [B25044](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25044). Households, not people: a car-free household of four counts once.

table:columns.name: pct_hh_no_vehicle_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_hh_no_vehicle` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: pct_hh_no_vehicle_cv
table:columns.description: Coefficient of variation for `pct_hh_no_vehicle`: `moe / 1.645 / estimate`, rounded to 3 decimals — the standard error as a fraction of the estimate, with 1.645 converting the published 90% margin back to a standard error. A rule of thumb: under 0.12 reliable, 0.12–0.40 use with caution, over 0.40 unreliable. NULL when the estimate is NULL or 0, or the margin of error is NULL. Published on the headline statistics so a map can grey out the geographies whose value is swamped by its own error instead of drawing them as if certain.

table:columns.name: pct_commute_drive_alone
table:columns.description: Percent of workers who drove alone to work in a car, truck or van. Universe: workers 16 years and over. Line 3 ("Drove alone", under "Car, truck, or van") over line 1 of [B08301](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B08301) (Means of Transportation to Work). The ACS asks about the usual means of transportation in the reference week, so a hybrid commuter reports one mode.

table:columns.name: pct_commute_drive_alone_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_commute_drive_alone` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. table:columns.name: pct_commute_transit

Line 10 ("Public transportation") over line 1 of [B08301](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B08301), which covers bus, subway and elevated rail, light rail, commuter rail and ferryboat. Taxi and ride-hailing (line 16) are a separate category in this vintage and are **not** included.

table:columns.name: pct_commute_walk_bike
table:columns.description: Percent of workers who walked or bicycled to work. Universe: workers 16 years and over. Lines 18 ("Bicycle") + 19 ("Walked") over line 1 of [B08301](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B08301).

table:columns.name: pct_work_from_home
table:columns.description: Percent of workers who worked from home. Universe: workers 16 years and over. Line 21 ("Worked from home") over line 1 of [B08301](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B08301). In a 2020–2024 5-year estimate this averages over the pandemic shift and its partial reversal, so it is not a reading of any single year.

Universe: workers 16 years and over **who did not work from home** — the table's own universe, which is why work-from-home does not deflate this share. Lines 11 + 12 + 13 (45 to 59 minutes, 60 to 89, 90 or more) over line 1 of [B08303](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B08303) (Travel Time to Work).

Households that use the internet without paying for a subscription (line 12) are counted as having access, so this is the floor of the digital divide, not its full extent.

table:columns.name: geometry
table:columns.description: Boundary polygon (Polygon or MultiPolygon), WKB-encoded, in EPSG:4326 / OGC:CRS84 — the GeoParquet default CRS, written as an omitted `crs` key. From the Census Bureau's 2024 cartographic boundary place file (GENZ2024, 1:500,000), which clips to the shoreline — TIGER/Line would extend the place into open water. Generalized for mapping and point-in-polygon work, not for legal-boundary or precise-area work.
